side_a: CC 3.4.11 "A consumer resolving an identity's age-assurance MUST union both prefixes and take the **highest** level on record. A witness-emitted `age_assurance:*` (provider/government) **OUTRANKS** a subject `age_self_declared:*`."
side_b: CC 3.4.13 "`age_self_declared:band:minor:v1` suffices. A child MUST NEVER be forced through provider/government assurance merely to be protected. This is a down-ratchet only: self-declaration MAY lower access / raise protection"
note: A provider row says adult and the person declares minor (a child on an adult-assured identity; the band is the identity's across the roster). CC 3.4.11 and the CC 3.1.2 row read adult: the witness outranks. CC 3.4.13 Q3 reads protected: a declaration alone enters protection and may lower. The fold cell follows 3.4.11 (pick=rank(government>provider>self)); formal/age_assurance follows 3.4.13 ('a declaration can lower the band and never raise it'). CC 3.4.11 wants the lowering stated. Confidence medium.

side_a: CC 3.2 "a minor has at most one live guardian, transferred by `supersedes`, never accreted"
side_b: CC 3.4.13 "M-of-N co-guardianship is supported as a verified DAG over `delegates_to` (guardianship clause, [CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)). The minor is never orphaned while ≥1 live adult guardian remains."
note: Open with the steward (held): one guardian per minor in CC 3.2 against a set of guardians with M-of-N rules in CC 3.4.13 Q7. Reported because a store built to CC 3.2 refuses the second binding Q7 requires.

side_a: CC 3.4.13 "So a person with no assurance on record uses their own and their family's scopes freely, and acts at community scope only with a guardian's co-sign"
side_b: CC 3.2 "**No minor `user` identity operates without a live adult steward.**"
note: Still present: no assurance reads as under_13, and 'each finer band implies `minor`'; CC 3.2 and CC 3.4.13 Q4 ('a guardian-less minor goes dark for general operation') stop a minor with no live guardian, while the fail-secure paragraph lets the unassured person use self and family scopes. The fail-secure paragraph limits only the announce refusal to 'a row on record'; CC 3.2 has no such limit.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 "the witness rung outranks the self rung, and the gate's default is protective"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json age_self_declared:band:{band}:{version} signer_rule: who any_registered, via none, conditions []
note: Still present: the signer cell admits any registered key to declare a band for a subject; the text admits the subject's own occurrence only.

side_a: CC 3.1.2 "Witness rung of the age ladder — `{level}` ∈ `provider` \| `government` (closed; `self` is refused here)"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version} signer_rule: seat_role(attest) via delegates_to(infra:attest_assurance), not_subject
note: Still present: the cell records the shipped store's delegated scope where the text gates on the witness identity_type; infra:attest_assurance is outside the closed infra:* set (C483).

side_a: CC 3.2 "the halt latch **as it reaches this node** ([CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md): a live accord edge at the halt's `asserted_at`)"
side_b: CC 4.2.1 "A halt is active at a node from the instant the node's store admits the row and latches ([CC 4.2.1.1](#4.2.1.1)). The signer-chosen `asserted_at` plays no part"
note: T8's inputs list restates the halt's reach at the signer's asserted_at; the home judges the edge at the node's own latch and says asserted_at plays no part. A node that cut its edge after the halt was signed and before it arrived is bound under T8's wording and free under CC 4.2.1; a sealed halt signed long ago flips the other way. This is the wording C033 records as removed from CC 4.2.1; it survives in CC 3.2. CC 4.2.1, 4.2.1.1 and 4.4.3.8 support the latch.

side_a: CC 4.2 "it reaches exactly those holding a live trust edge to the accord when it is fired"
side_b: CC 4.2.1 "A `constitutional` halt binds exactly the nodes holding a **live `delegates_to(user → accord)`** at the instant the halt becomes active at that node."
note: CC 4.2 judges the edge 'when it is fired', which reads as the signer's act; the home judges it per node at the latch. The next sentence of CC 4.2 ('a halt latched before the cut') agrees with the home, so a careful reader lands there.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 "Every `accord:invoke:*` Contribution signs the canonical bytes below."
side_b: CC 5.3.2.4.2 "The signature MUST cover `JCS(contribution_envelope)` — the **identical** canonical bytes any natively-federation attestation signs."
note: Still present: CC 4.2.1.1 has a halt row's signature over the labelled sha256 preimage; CC 2.6.1.7 and CC 5.3.2.4.2 put every row signature over JCS of the envelope and nothing else. One verifier refuses the other's halt. No typed member carries an inner signature.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED" (the presence cell of `scrub_signature_classical`; the gloss cell reads "Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over JCS(attestation_envelope)")
side_b: CC 5.3.2.4.3 "MAY be absent (deferred per CC 5.3.2.2)" (the Signature cell of the `local` tier)
note: The signed-object table (and the CDDL) makes the Ed25519 half REQUIRED with no tier condition, and only the ML-DSA half 'REQUIRED at the federation tier'. CC 5.3.2.2 and 5.3.2.4.5 have a local row skip both halves ('unsigned'). A store built from the table refuses a local row with no classical half. Part 5 is the home of the tiers; the table's cell wants the same tier condition.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.2 "The signature MUST cover `JCS(contribution_envelope)`"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over JCS(attestation_envelope); RFC 4648 section 4 standard alphabet, padded."
note: Two names for one signed object: `contribution_envelope` occurs once in the document (CC 5.3.2.4.2), `attestation_envelope` is the name CC 2.6.1.7 and the CDDL define; CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 writes `JCS(envelope)`. A careful reader resolves to attestation_envelope.

side_a: CC 3.1.2 "Each `BuildManifest` is hybrid-signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) by the per-primitive steward."
side_b: CC 3.1.2.1 "signed by the pipeline that built it, citing the manifest's bytes from `evidence_refs[]`"
note: Still present (held): CC 3.1.2 names a steward as signer; CC 3.1.2.1 and the signer cell (any_registered) have the building pipeline sign and the reader judge its standing.

side_a: CC 4.2.6 "They are **never** published in the GenesisBundle's `holders`, which is the accord-family roster"
side_b: CC 4.2.2 "carried as a JSON property inside the `attestation_evidence` of a signed key record, as served in the GenesisBundle's `holders` / `serve_nodes`"
note: Still present (proposed, not applied): CC 4.2.6 keeps the accord holders' PQC halves out of the bundle's `holders`; CC 4.2.2 and CC 5.3.4 serve the holders' signed key records there, and CC 4.2.1.1 has an agent verify a holder's hybrid signature against the pinned roster. An agent built to CC 4.2.6 alone cannot verify a halt from the bundle.

side_a: CC 3.1.1 "A `steward_purge` notice is a **cosigned row** ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)): `attesting_key_id` is the seat that proposes it"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json takedown_notice:{basis} attest: roles ["takedown"], policy selfAct, one transition for every basis
note: Still present: the text has a steward_purge notice cosigned under the root's consensus_protocol, proposed by any seat of the root; the data has one attest transition for every basis, one voice, role takedown (the family_model cosign cell records the gap and holds it shut).

side_a: CC 3.2 "the head de-witnessed (its counted witnesses revoked before their `signed_at`, or the directory collapsed to non-independent keys)"
side_b: CC 3.2 "A consumer that holds a witnessed head MUST refuse a competing head that is not witnessed"
note: T8 lists a directory collapse among the NotRooted cases and as a transition (a new witnessed head that removes a leg -> NotRooted). T6 judges independence at the cosignature's signed_at ('a later change of role neither voids an earlier cosignature'), verifies a head against its parent's directory, and has the holder refuse an unwitnessed head; T4/T4a say nothing but a revocation detaches an attached node. One reader detaches every attached node at the collapse; the other keeps them Rooted on the last witnessed head. T4 and the nearest-verifying-ancestor input support the second. Confidence medium.

side_a: CC 3.2 "the halt latch **as it reaches this node** ([CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md): a live accord edge at the halt's `asserted_at`)"
side_b: CC 3.2 "A `constitutional` halt moves no state here: *V* at *t* is the same with and without a latched halt, whatever roster rows land between"
note: T8 names the halt latch as an input of V, and invariant (v), T3 and the transitions paragraph say V never reads it. An input that cannot change the output; a reader of the inputs list alone could condition the verdict on the latch. The invariant governs.

side_a: CC 4.4.1 "Consumers SHOULD apply identity-prejudice-resistant weighting."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.10 "`cw_class:*` declarations from low-attestation-density cohorts MUST NOT be downweighted; they ride alongside the gate decision as informational."
note: CC 4.4.3.10 states as MUST NOT, 'layered with CC 4.4.1', a rule whose home is a SHOULD and whose bullets name testimonial_witness and non_maleficence, not cw_class. CC 3.3.12 gives it no keyword. One force is wanted; the home is CC 4.4.1.

side_a: CC 4.4.1 "per [CC 3.4.7](part_3_the_namespace.md) the consumer MUST also weight `witness_relation: self` claims against the attester's other-emission track record"
side_b: CC 2.1 "Consumers weight by relation, so that self-attestation cannot game a verdict."
note: CC 4.4.1 gives a MUST and cites CC 3.4.7, which is the reserved-prefix admission rule and says nothing of witness_relation weighting or a track record. The only other statement is CC 2.1's unkeyworded sentence, with no track-record test. The MUST has no home.

side_a: CC 4.2.2 "Interim value before actual hardware provisioning. Consumers MUST treat as `0.0` trust weight"
side_b: CC 4.2.2 "Per-class recommended trust-multipliers: `HSM_FIPS_140_3_L3` = 1.0; `Apple_Secure_Enclave` = 0.95; `YubiKey_5_FIPS` = 0.95; `TPM_2_0` = 0.9; `placeholder_pending_provisioning` = 0.0"
note: The table makes 0.0 for the placeholder a MUST and rejection of software_hsm_development a MUST; the next paragraph lists both as recommended multipliers of 0.0, and CC 2.2 calls both a 'rejection'. A zero multiplier and a refusal are different acts in a mean. The table's MUST is the stricter and CC 2.2 supports it.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.11 "The combination is the consumer-side recipe for "fresh AND logged AND verified at ladder position L3 or above.""
side_b: CC 4.4.3.11 "`cert_validity:{authority} + transparency_log:inclusion + (attestation:registry_consensus OR attestation:license_validity)`"
note: By CC 4.4.3.6 the ladder verdict is the highest rung with a positive attestation, so a subject holding only attestation:agent_integrity is at L5, 'L3 or above', and fails the formula, which accepts L3 or L4 only. The formula is the stated pattern.

side_a: CC 3.4.12 "The age rule resolves *absence of an age attestation* protectively to `minor` ([CC 3.4.11](part_3_the_namespace.md))."
side_b: CC 3.4.11 "Absence of any row resolves to **None**, which MUST be treated as the most-protective band, `under_13`"
note: Still present in CC 3.4.12's gloss: the ruled default is under_13 with co-sign (CC 3.4.11, 3.4.13); CC 3.4.12 still reports it as `minor`.

side_a: CC 3.2 "The acceptance edge is a person's row: any live key of the person's roster signs it as that person"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json trust:{job}:{version} signer_rule: "accepts: self (node -> root)"; CC 8.10 card: authorize | self
note: Still present: the signer cell and the CC 8.10 card still read the acceptance edge as the node's own.

side_a: CC 3.2 "Un-trust is therefore **one deletion**. Remove the acceptance edge and every downstream gate fails closed **emergently**"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json trust:{job}:{version} withdraw: roles author, subject; policy selfAct (CC 8.10 card: withdraw | author, subject)
note: Still present: one withdraw transition for every job, open to the subject. For accepts the subject is the root, which could then withdraw an owner's acceptance; for the cosigned charter a single signer could withdraw. The text gives the edge to the owner and the charter to its quorum.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.8 "Present, it is a non-empty, sorted, deduplicated list of class ids, and an empty list is refused. `trust_depth` is `0..5`."
side_b: data manifests/signed_object.cddl: "? trust_classes: [* tstr]" and "? trust_depth: uint"
note: The CDDL admits an empty trust_classes and any unsigned trust_depth; the text refuses [] (trust_accepts_classes_malformed) and a depth above 5 (trust_accepts_depth_out_of_range). The CDDL wants [+ tstr] and 0..5.

side_a: CC 5.4.6 "Each node's setup chooses whether that node **announces**, which in this section means one thing: its owner-binding ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)) is carried at `cohort_scope: federation`"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "Every node announces its identity destination, so an observer sees that each member node exists and is reachable."
note: Still present (proposed, not applied): the section fixes 'announces' to the federation-scope owner-binding, then uses the bare verb for the Reticulum broadcast in the observer paragraph, where 'every node' would include the unannounced, a recorded minor's node and the anonymous node that 'announces nothing'. The transport sense is meant there.

side_a: CC 5.4.6 "**Un-announcing** is the owner superseding the binding at `cohort_scope: self` and withdrawing the grants that carried it to the roots they trust, one act in the client."
side_b: CC 3.2 "The re-signed row is a second owner-signed row beside the `self` one, never a replacement, and the audience rule of its tier places it."
note: Still present (held): CC 5.4.6 un-announces by a supersedes at self scope; CC 3.2 keeps the federation row as a second row that nothing at self replaces, so the federation row must itself be withdrawn. One store keeps a live federation binding after an un-announce. CC 5.4.6's own 'a withdrawn binding stops satisfying it' supports CC 3.2.
